prompt: Complete the Counter class so a static field tracks how many instances have been created, while each instance remembers its own 1-based creation order id.
explanation: A static field belongs to the class itself, so every Counter object shares the same instanceCount; incrementing it in the constructor counts every object ever created. The id is an instance field, so each object keeps its own copy captured at construction time. Static methods like getInstanceCount() and resetCount() read and write the shared field without needing any particular instance.
hints: A field declared with the static keyword is shared by all instances of the class; a normal instance field is separate for each object.
In the constructor, increment the static count first, then store its new value into the instance's final id field.
resetCount() only sets the static count back to 0 -- ids already handed out do not change.
